statement: A uniform bound P(X_n<=t)<=(1+1/n)t for all t>=0 does not imply the existence of c,C>0 with P(X_n<=t)<=t+C exp(-c n) for all n,t>=0, even for nonnegative random variables with continuous distribution functions.
proof: F_n(t)=min((1+1/n)t,1) for t>=0. At t=1/n, n>=2, F_n(t)-t=1/n^2. For every c,C>0, 1/n^2>C exp(-c n) for all sufficiently large n.
counterexample_scope: Refutes an implication from a multiplicative near-one bound alone; it is not a counterexample to the Bernoulli matrix conjecture.
remaining_gap: Independent referee and response-side served-model evidence pending; no Bernoulli-matrix-specific proof attempted yet.

statement: For independent Z~N(0,1) and almost surely finite R>=0, h(t)=P(|Z|<=tR) satisfies h(t)>=(t/t0)h(t0) for 0<t<=t0. If E[R^3]<infinity the excess is at most sqrt(2/pi)*t*(t0^2-t^2)*E[R^3]/6.
assumptions: Z is a real standard Gaussian
R is nonnegative, finite almost surely and independent of Z
E[R^3]<infinity is needed only for the quantitative upper bound
proof: Condition on R and substitute u=t*v in the Gaussian density integral. The integrand exp(-t^2*v^2/2) decreases in t. Use exp(-a)-exp(-b)<=b-a for 0<=a<=b and integrate v^2 from 0 to R.
remaining_gap: Independent referee and response-side served-model evidence pending. Does not settle C0029.

statement: Conditional finiteness of the Gaussian rescaling-radius third moment does not imply unconditional finiteness: for independent A,B,W~N(0,1), R=abs(W)/(sqrt(2)*sqrt(A^2+B^2)) has E[R^3]=infinity although E[R^3|A,B]<infinity almost surely.
assumptions: A,B,W are independent standard real Gaussians
proof: sqrt(A^2+B^2) has density r exp(-r^2/2); its negative third moment diverges like integral_0^1 r^(-2)dr. Independence factors the nonnegative moment; the numerator has finite positive third moment.
remaining_gap: Small-dimensional missing-premise counterexample only; no asymptotic Bernoulli theorem. Independent check pending.
